title: Alibaba Cloud's Full-Stack AI Compute Self-Development Emerges: Zhenwu V900 Chip Set for Mass Production Next Year, Supernode Power Draw Reaches 650kW
key_facts: Alibaba Cloud showed its full-stack in-house AI hardware at the recent Apsara Conference, from chips to rack-level clusters.
The Zhenwu V900 has 216GB of memory, 1200GB/s chip-to-chip bandwidth and FP8/FP4 support, and delivers three times the performance of the previous M890; mass production is slated for Q1 2027.
Chips come from T-Head Semiconductor, Alibaba Group's wholly owned chip design company set up in 2018.
Alibaba builds hardware for its own cloud and rents it out, unlike Huawei which sells Ascend and Kunpeng products externally.
The flagship Panjiu AL144 supernode (up to 144 GPUs per rack) draws 650kW per rack and is fully liquid-cooled.
China's intelligent computing services market was about 68.4 billion yuan in 2025 and is projected to exceed 277.5 billion yuan by 2030 (CIC data).
quote_evidence: Among data center compute chips, the Zhenwu series is the undisputed workhorse.
According to the roadmap, the Zhenwu V900 is slated for mass production in Q1 2027.

To support such immense compute density, the AL144 draws a staggering 650kW per rack, supports up to 3,500W per GPU, and employs an 800V vertical power architecture with vertical jet impingement microchannel cold plates — a fully liquid-cooled native design.
why_it_matters_hint: Alibaba is building a complete Chinese alternative stack of AI chips, servers and networks for its own cloud.
